summary: Phase 2 (Site Engineer restoration + PO threshold approval chain) backend regression. 40/40 in-scope tests PASSED (100%) on first run — no code fixes required. Every case in the review request is verified: full E2E happy path (steps 2-14, incl. Site Engineer -> PM -> Purchase -> GM/Director gates), threshold settings CRUD (15-19), role visibility for MRFs/POs/Projects (20-26), and cross-role denials (27-30). PO threshold logic works exactly as specified: total <= 50000 -> issued; 50000 < total <= 500000 -> pending_gm_approval; total > 500000 -> pending_director_approval. MRF qty_ordered is deferred until PO is approved (verified 0 -> 5 after GM approve). GRN endpoint (/po/{id}/received) returns 400 while PO is pending_gm/director_approval or rejected. GM correctly denied on director-tier PO (403). Site engineer now first-class in dev-login and can create/submit MRFs and record GRN on POs originating from own MRFs. Threshold PUT enforces director >= gm (400 on violation) and is restricted to director/admin. Ran alongside 43 additional legacy tests: 4 pre-existing stale-assertion failures in test_phase1_role_reshuffle.py/test_phase1_followup.py are consistent with Phase 2 (site_engineer is no longer invalid/legacy; pm is now in GRN_ROLES) — these should be refreshed by the main agent but are NOT regressions.
action_items: STALE TEST CLEANUP (non-blocking): Update 4 assertions that pre-date Phase 2 role reshuffle: (a) test_phase1_role_reshuffle.py::TestNewRoles::test_invalid_role_rejected now passes 'site_engineer' expecting 400 but Phase 2 accepts it (200). (b) TestLegacyMigration::test_site_engineer_migrates_to_pm expects site_engineer->pm migration, but Phase 2 removed that mapping (site_engineer is first-class). (c) TestPOReceived::test_pm_forbidden and test_phase1_followup.py::TestPOReceivedRoles::test_pm_403 expect PM 403 on /po/received but Phase 2 added 'pm' to GRN_ROLES per operational chain. Fix by updating expected values to reflect Phase 2 spec.

Docstring drift in server.py line 43-44: comment says 'Admin is a system-management role and NOT part of the approval chain by default' but require_roles() has a global admin bypass. This is intentional per the code review (admin has admin-override powers on data), but the comment could be clarified so it matches behavior.

Consider extracting the 4 role-tuple sets (MRF_APPROVERS, MRF_EDITORS, MRF_CREATORS, GRN_ROLES) into named module-level constants that are then reused in `require_roles(*...)` calls at lines 700, 858, 921, 942, 1035, 1134, 1250, 1282, etc. Currently the same tuples are re-declared inline at every endpoint, which is where the bug class of duplicated/omitted role tuples (fixed 3 times in previous iterations) originates.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:78 `_po_initial_status()` uses strict > comparators consistent with the spec (total ≤ GM -> issued; GM < total ≤ Director -> pending_gm; total > Director -> pending_director). Verified with 10_000 (issued), 100_000 (pending_gm), 1_000_000 (pending_director), all with GST=0/freight=0 to make math deterministic.
server.py:1064-1081 correctly defers MRF item qty_ordered rollup until PO is approved. Verified: mid PO leaves MRF qty_ordered=0 while pending_gm_approval, then jumps to full qty after GM approve.
server.py:1047-1048 correctly blocks GM from approving director-tier POs with 403; but allows director to approve either tier (which is spec-correct).

server.py:1139 GRN endpoint correctly returns 400 when po.status is pending_gm_approval / pending_director_approval / rejected — before the _check_po_access check runs (so a SE calling GRN on a pending PO gets 400, not 403, matching the spec).
server.py:1443-1466 PUT /settings/thresholds enforces director/admin (403), numeric validation, non-negative, and director >= gm (400). Full 4-way validation coverage.

server.py:344-372 /auth/dev-login accepts site_engineer as first-class; legacy 'site_engineer' is no longer in LEGACY_ROLE_MAP (server.py:46-53), so a legacy-persisted site_engineer stays site_engineer. Migration comment inside dev_login is now truthful.
